dns.extension.name: DNS
dns.extension.description: Name servers, DNSSEC and CAA records of the domain.
dns.nameservers.title: Name servers
dns.nameservers.why: Name servers answer for the domain to the whole Internet. With only one, if it fails, the website and the mail disappear at the same time.
dns.nameservers.ref: RFC 2182 (at least two servers, on separate networks)
dns.nameservers.ok: {count} name servers answer for the zone {zone}.
dns.nameservers.single: A single name server for the zone {zone}: {host}.
dns.nameservers.none: No name server found for this name or its parent domains: this check does not apply.
dns.nameservers.message:
Hello,

The domain {domain} is served by a single name server ({host}). If it fails, the website and the mail become unreachable.

Could you add at least a second name server, hosted on another network?

Thank you.
dns.dnssec.title: DNSSEC signature
dns.dnssec.why: DNSSEC signs the answers of the DNS, so nobody can send visitors or e-mail to a fake server by forging them.
dns.dnssec.ref: RFC 4033 · ANSSI, « Bonnes pratiques pour l'acquisition et l'exploitation de noms de domaine »
dns.dnssec.on: The zone {zone} is signed with DNSSEC.
dns.dnssec.off: The zone {zone} is not signed with DNSSEC.
dns.dnssec.how: At most DNS hosts, DNSSEC is one switch in the domain settings, with nothing to type. The host publishes the keys and keeps them up to date.
dns.dnssec.broken: The zone {zone} is declared signed (DS record) but does not publish its keys: resolvers that check DNSSEC may refuse its answers.
dns.dnssec.broken_message:
Hello,

The zone {zone} is declared signed with DNSSEC (a DS record is published) but publishes no DNSKEY key. Resolvers that check DNSSEC may stop resolving the domain.

Could you publish the keys again, or remove the DS record at the registrar?

Thank you.
dns.caa.title: Allowed certificate authorities (CAA)
dns.caa.why: A CAA record names the only authorities allowed to issue a certificate for the domain. The others refuse, which makes a forged certificate harder to obtain.
dns.caa.present: CAA records name the allowed authorities.
dns.caa.missing: No CAA record: any authority may issue a certificate for the domain.
dns.caa.how: The proposed value allows {ca}, the authority that issued the website's current certificate. If another service also gets certificates for the domain (mail, online shop), add a record for it too.
dns.caa.present_inherited: The CAA records of {zone} name the allowed authorities, for this name too.
dns.caa.excludes_current: The CAA records do not allow {ca}, the authority that issued the current certificate ({issuer}): its next renewal will be refused.
dns.caa.excludes_current.action: Allow the authority of the current certificate
dns.caa.excludes_current.how: Add a CAA record "0 issue "{ca}"" next to the existing ones, or move to another authority before the certificate expires.
